items.question: Tell me about yourself.
items.text: I am a good student and I work hard.

items.question: Why are you interested in this role?
items.text: I am interested in this role because I want to learn data analysis. In my final-year project I analysed 2 years of college placement data in Python and built a dashboard that the placement cell now uses. I enjoyed finding patterns that changed a real decision, and this role lets me do that every day with bigger datasets.

items.question: What is your biggest weakness?
items.text: Um, I think, you know, I am basically a perfectionist, I mean I like everything to be perfect, so that is kind of my weakness I guess and yeah that is basically it.

items.question: What is your biggest weakness?
items.text: My weakness is public speaking. During my second year I froze in a seminar, so I joined the college debate club and spoke at 6 events last year. I am still nervous, but I now prepare an outline first because it keeps me on track, and my last seminar score improved from 12 to 17 out of 20.

items.question: Tell me about a conflict with a teammate.
items.text: We had some conflict but we talked and everything became fine in the end.

items.question: Tell me about a conflict with a teammate.
items.text: In my final-year project, a teammate and I disagreed about the database. I wanted PostgreSQL because our data was relational, while he preferred MongoDB. I built a small test of our 3 main queries on both, and I shared the results with the team. Because the joins were 4 times faster on PostgreSQL, he agreed, and as a result we delivered the project two weeks early. I learned that data ends arguments faster than opinions.

items.question: Describe a time you failed to meet a deadline.
items.text: During my internship I missed a report deadline by one day. I had underestimated the data cleaning. I told my manager as soon as I knew, and I then started splitting my tasks into daily goals.

items.question: Describe a time you led a group.
items.text: We organised the tech fest and we all worked very hard together and the whole team did a really good job, everybody was happy and the event went well and people liked it a lot.

items.question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
items.text: A process is a program and a thread is smaller.

items.question: What is the difference between a process and a thread?
items.text: A process has its own memory space, whereas threads share the memory of their process. Because of that, switching between threads is cheaper, however a bug in one thread can crash the whole process. For example, in my Python project I used threads for 8 concurrent downloads, which spend most of their time waiting on the network, so sharing memory was simple and efficient. First the main thread queued the URLs, then the workers picked them up.

items.question: What is an index in a database?
items.text: An index makes queries faster because the database does not scan the whole table. It uses a B-tree, so lookups are logarithmic, however every insert must also update the index, which is the trade-off.

items.question: Explain TCP and UDP.
items.text: Um TCP is, you know, reliable and UDP is, uh, not reliable I think.
